answer: A bonded identity registry can resist Sybil attacks by making each agent lock a stake that is tied to one verified credential, so a hollow shell account cannot vote or trade. An attacker trying to cross the canyon between one identity and many must post a separate bond for every copy and risk slashing for fraud. The registry also keeps a mirror record of past work and peer ratings, so reputation cannot be cloned for free; building many credible fakes means paying many bonds, doing real work for each, and losing stake when any copy is caught.
